Execute only this independent PaperOrchestra invocation. Do not delegate or run the whole pipeline. You are an already dispatched role worker; model selection is complete. Do not invoke the PaperOrchestra setup flow or ask which model to use. Use only the supplied task inputs; return its requested output format verbatim. Do not read other invocation folders. Do not write workspace files.

You are an expert statistical plot illustrator. Write code to generate high-quality statistical plots based on user requests.

Use R with ggplot2 to generate a statistical plot based on the following detailed description: # Figure description: `fig_intercept_error`

## Content

**Chart type:** Point chart (scatter plot with three markers, no connecting line, no fitted curve, no error bars).

**Data (exactly three recorded pairs, each drawn as one point):**

| Point | b (x) | MSE (y) |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0 | 9 |
| 2 | 1.5 | 2.25 |
| 3 | 3 | 0 |

**Variable mapping:**
- **x channel:** added intercept correction `b`, the value added to `2x` (the baseline predictor). Ticks at 0, 1.5, 3.
- **y channel:** mean squared error, `mean((y - (2x + b))^2)` over the five observations. Ticks at 0, 3, 6, 9.
- **hue / shape:** none. All points share one color and one shape, since there is only one series.

**Provenance (for manuscript caption/text, not embedded in visual):** the five synthetic observations are (x, y) = (−2, −1), (−1, 1), (0, 3), (1, 5), (2, 7). Their residuals against `2x` are all 3, so the correction is `b = mean(y − 2x) = 3`. The MAE column (3, 1.5, 0) is in the source table but is not plotted.

**Text elements:**
- **Title:** "Recorded Mean Squared Error at Three Intercept Corrections"
- **x-axis label:** "Added intercept correction b"
- **y-axis label:** "Mean squared error (MSE)"
- **Point labels:** "9.00" (above point 1), "2.25" (above point 2), "0.00" (above point 3).
- **Caption:** Separate manuscript caption (excluded from visual canvas): "Figure: Recorded mean squared error across three candidate intercept corrections. Each point is a recorded result on the five synthetic observations (x, y) = (−2, −1), (−1, 1), (0, 3), (1, 5), (2, 7), which determine the correction b = mean(y − 2x) = 3 and evaluate it. The plot demonstrates finite arithmetic rather than predictive generalization. No held-out data, fitted curve, or uncertainty interval is shown."

## Presentation

- **Canvas:** 6.0 in × 4.0 in, white background (`#FFFFFF`).
- **Theme:** `theme_classic(base_size = 12)`, with the panel border removed.
- **Font family:** sans-serif (Helvetica or Arial), applied to all text elements.
- **Markers:** filled circles (`shape = 16`), size 4 (about 4 mm), color `#1F4E79` (dark blue), no outline.
- **Point labels:** 10 pt, color `#333333`, `vjust = -1.2`.
- **Axis titles:** 12 pt, bold, color `#222222`.
- **Axis tick labels:** 10 pt, color `#444444`.
- **Title:** 13 pt, bold, left-aligned, color `#111111`.
- **Axis lines:** 0.5 pt, color `#444444`.
- **Grid:** horizontal major gridlines only, 0.3 pt, color `#E5E5E5`. No vertical gridlines and no minor gridlines.
- **Axis limits:** x from −0.3 to 3.3; y from −0.6 to 10.5.
- **Legend:** none.

## Reproducible R/ggplot2 source (described, not written to disk)

r
library(ggplot2)

# Recorded results only; no interpolation or extra measurements
df <- data.frame(
  b   = c(0, 1.5, 3),
  mse = c(9, 2.25, 0)
)

p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = b, y = mse)) +
  geom_point(shape = 16, size = 4, colour = "#1F4E79") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", mse)),
            vjust = -1.2, size = 3.5, colour = "#333333") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 1.5, 3), limits = c(-0.3, 3.3)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, 3, 6, 9), limits = c(-0.6, 10.5)) +
  labs(
    title = "Recorded Mean Squared Error at Three Intercept Corrections",
    x     = "Added intercept correction b",
    y     = "Mean squared error (MSE)"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title         = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold", colour = "#111111", hjust = 0),
    axis.title         = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", colour = "#222222"),
    axis.text          = element_text(size = 10, colour = "#444444"),
    axis.line          = element_line(linewidth = 0.5, colour = "#444444"),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(linewidth = 0.3, colour = "#E5E5E5"),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    legend.position    = "none",
    plot.margin        = margin(t = 10, r = 15, b = 10, l = 10, unit = "pt")
  )

# Vector PDF (editable, reproducible) and manuscript-compatible preview
ggsave("fig_intercept_error.pdf", p, device = cairo_pdf, width = 6, height = 4)
ggsave("fig_intercept_error_preview.png", p, width = 6, height = 4, dpi = 300)


## Output artifacts

- `fig_intercept_error.R`: the source above, saved as an editable script.
- `fig_intercept_error.pdf`: vector output for the manuscript.
- `fig_intercept_error_preview.png`: 300 dpi raster preview.
Return R code only. Define the final ggplot object as p. Do not save files: the rendering wrapper exports p to PDF and JPEG. Use only base R and ggplot2, with built-in serif, sans or mono font families. Use the supplied numeric data exactly; do not simulate or invent observations. Do not install packages or download data. The runtime sets set.seed(0). Requested canvas aspect ratio: 4:3. Code:
